questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

Madhuri and I have done my (1)/ work patiently and diligently (2)/ just for our safe and secure future. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution:
The correct** answer is option 1**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c8c9521921258ec6abc07d0cc2f42f7e8a9f276861eb6ba131097c2c69c56057.png] Let's look at the following points-**

 
• The subject clause of the sentence contains Madhuri and I which means it is a **plural noun**
 
• As the** subject** is **plural** hence **the verb and the pronoun** (if any in a sentence) must be followed in the** plural form**
 
• In the given sentence possessive pronoun** 'my'** is given which is "**first person singular possessive pronoun**"
 
• Hence**, 'my' **will be replaced with** 'our'** which is ''**first-person Plural possessive pronoun**''

​**Thus, the correct sentence is-**Madhuri and I have done our work patiently and diligently just for our safe and secure future.

​​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7aa83af99ce472524089f105a39231d420512e90e6e735e1c21953d903076977.png] **Extra- Bite-**

** Possessive pronoun** for all three persons are**- **

 
 

 **SINGULAR**
 **PLURAL**
 
 

 My, Mine
 our, ours
 
 

 Your, Yours
 Your, yours
 
 

 His, her. hers, its
 Their, theirs
 
 

34:T

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

I don’t think, Neha is a wise as (1)/ Sonali, so she is not (2)/ competent for this job. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer **is option 1**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c8c9521921258ec6abc07d0cc2f42f7e8a9f276861eb6ba131097c2c69c56057.png] Let's look at the following points-**

 
• In the first part of the sentence **'a' **will be replaced by **'as'**; since conjunction** 'as........as'** is used for comparing one person, thing or situation with another
 
• let's see the following structure-

​ subject (1) + Verb + as/so + positive degree + as +subject (2)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7aa83af99ce472524089f105a39231d420512e90e6e735e1c21953d903076977.png] ** Important-point**

 
• For Affirmative sentences we use - **as + positive degree + as **
 
• For Negative sentence we can use both- **as + positive degree + as **or **so + positive degree +as**
 
• **For e.g.- **He is **as intelligent as **you.

** **He is not **so /as intelligent as** you.

***Correct sentence - **I don’t think, Neha is** as wise as **Sonali, so she is not competent for this job.*

We must (1)/ denounce justice (2)/ and oppression. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution: The correct** answer is option 2** ** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c8c9521921258ec6abc07d0cc2f42f7e8a9f276861eb6ba131097c2c69c56057.png] Let's look at the following points-** • **Denounce** means publicly declare something to be wrong or evil; criticize, condemn. (आरोप लगा देना; सार्वजनिक रूप से कुछ गलत या बुरा घोषित करना; आलोचना करना, निंदा करना) • **Oppression** means prolonged cruel or unjust treatment or exercise of authority; Persecution, maltreatment. (उत्पीड़न) • According to the context of the sentence, **injustice** (lack of fairness or justice) will be the correct word, as we cannot** criticize or denounce** 'justice' • Hence, **'justice'** will be replaced by** 'injustice'** to make the sentence correct *The Correct sentence - We must denounce injustice and oppression. * 36:T93f, The correct answer **is option 1**

questions.question:
**Improve the bracketed part of the sentence.**

(No sooner I saw) the lizard than I ran away.
questions.solution:
**Correct option - 3**

Here, concept of **no sooner....than** conjunction is brought under consideration. Since, the verb used after this conjunction depends upon the form of tense used further in the sentence. Since, **ran **is a simple past tense's verb, hence similar tense to be followed. Thus, options 1 & 2 are clearly eliminated. Now, when such conjunction is used with simple past tense, then helping verb **did **is used. Hence, option 3 is the correct answer.

**Correct sentence - **No sooner did I see the lizard than I ran away.
